slides.title: Microservices
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.
defs: An architecture that divides an application into smaller independently deployable services communicating through interfaces/APIs.

slides.title: Key Concepts
slides.raw:
Key Concepts
• Modularity
• Independence
• Decentralized Data Management
• Autonomous Development and
Deployment
• APIs for Communication
slides.teach: These points define the technology. Be able to explain each one in your own words and recognize it in a scenario.

course.learn: This section focuses on **Key Concepts** within **Microservices**. Microservices divide an application into smaller independently deployable services that communicate through APIs or messaging.
course.why: Smaller services can improve scalability and isolation, but they create many service-to-service identities, APIs, and network paths that must be secured.
course.example: An e-commerce app has separate services for catalog, payment, orders, and shipping, each authenticated to the others.
course.exam: Think API security, service identity, secrets, east-west traffic, observability, and segmentation.
